messages:
jane_support: Customer on private deployment (vpc-12a) is seeing 503s and intermittent TLS handshake failures when hitting our private API gateway since they flipped ExpressRoute authorization key this morning. They also report DNS resolution sometimes timing out.

mike_net: ugh. any error samples from the gateway or tls logs?

jane_support: pasted error from gateway: `tls: handshake failure: remote error: handshake failure` and API logs show: `upstream connect error or disconnect` + `dial tcp: lookup svc.internal: no such host` intermittently.

sam_peering: timeline? did the customer rotate auth key or update route filters?

jane_support: customer says they rotated the ExpressRoute authorization key at 09:12, then at 09:40 they started seeing failures. BGP sessions mostly up but a few short flaps reported.

mike_net: ask them for BGP neighbor state and route table on their edge. also need tcpdump around 4500/500 and 443 to see if DNS/TLS reach the egress.

jane_support: requested pcap and bgp neigh, they're uploading now. shared gist link when ready.

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-4392 (Priority: P2) — assigned to net-eng.

sam_peering: two quick hypotheses: 1) authorization change triggered an Azure route-filter/peering update preventing some egress to CRL/OCSP responders (causes cert verification failures). 2) MTU/MSS issue on IPsec/ExpressRoute causing TLS fragments to drop -> handshake error.

emma_oncall: +1 on MTU. If DF set and fragments dropped you'll see STARTTLS/ClientHello but no ServerHello. Also DNS timeouts could be because UDP fragmentation is being dropped.

mike_net: can we confirm whether the customer's NAT/NGW or route table now forces egress through a firewall that blocks outbound 443 to endpoints like `ocsp.digicert.com`, `crl.exampleCA.com`, or DNS to 8.8.8.8? Ask them for their firewall egress allowlist rules.

jane_support: customer posted firewall rules: egress only allows 443 to a short whitelist (internal proxies), DNS to 10.0.0.2 only. No explicit allow to public OCSP or CRL. They said proxy was updated by security team after auth key rotation.

sam_peering: that matches. Certificate validation will fail if OCSP/CRL unreachable — some clients treat that as hard fail. Also if proxy does TLS intercept without proper certs it can break SNI-based routing.

mike_net: repro steps we asked customer to run (asked them to run and return logs):
```
# on app host
dig +short svc.internal @10.0.0.2
curl -v --resolve api.internal:443:10.0.0.5 https://api.internal/health
sudo tcpdump -nni any host 10.0.0.5 and (port 443 or port 53 or portrange 500-4500) -w /tmp/express.pcap
ip route show
sudo sysctl net.ipv4.ip_forward
```

jane_support: they ran dig and got intermittent NXDOMAIN, curl hung and then TLS handshake error, attached pcap.

mike_net: downloaded pcap. quick notes: seeing many TCP retransmits and several ICMP fragmentation-needed (type 3 code 4) from next-hop 192.168.100.1 to the app host. MSS advertised 1460 and packets >1400 are being dropped. Also several UDP DNS requests get no reply.

sam_peering: so MTU/MSS path problem. Likely the ExpressRoute/edge or firewall did not apply MSS clamping on ESP/UDP-encapsulated packets after the auth change. IPsec encaps adds overhead -> needs lower MSS on inner TCP.

emma_oncall: mitigation: enable MSS clamping on the customer's NAT/firewall or on the virtual appliance in front of peering. Alternatively set PMTU/MSS on host: `sudo iptables -t mangle -A FORWARD -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --set-mss 1200` (quick patch). Also ensure outbound allowlist includes OCSP/CRL and DNS endpoints.

jane_support: forwarded mitigation to customer; security team is hesitant to open public OCSP endpoints. they asked if we can make gateway skip OCSP for their tenant (temporary).

mike_net: we can't disable OCSP globally. Work with customer: 1) permit OCSP/CRL egress to the specific responders used by their CA, 2) apply MSS clamping on the firewall, 3) confirm NAT/Proxy does not break SNI or CT logs.

sam_peering: also check Azure ExpressRoute peering config: route filter prefix lists could have been narrowed during auth key rotation if they re-provisioned peering. ask them to run `az network express-route peering show --name <peering> --resource-group <rg>` and share `authorizationKey` state & `peerings` output.

jane_support: customer applied MSS clamping to 1200 on firewall and temporarily allowed OCSP endpoints. after change they report API health OK and no TLS handshake failures for 18 minutes. closing loop with security to review permanent policy.

emma_oncall: leave incident open till 24h stable, but sounds like primary cause MTU + egress allowlist. please add runbook note on adding MSS clamping as a remediation for ExpressRoute+IPsec private peerings.

jane_support: agreed — adding runbook entry and tagging net-eng. thanks team :thumbsup:

mike_net: will follow up with a postmortem template entry: cause=proxy+auth-change removed clamping, effect=MTU fragmentation -> DNS/TLS failures, mitigation=clamp MSS + allow OCSP+CRL.

infra-bot: Incident INC-4392 updated: status -> monitoring.
